content: Professor Alison Kitson, RN, BSc (Hons), PhD, FRCN, is a distinguished nurse from the United Kingdom who currently leads the professional nursing agenda for the Royal College of Nursing (RCN). Previously, she served as the Director of the RCN Institute, where she played a pivotal role in advancing several innovative initiatives. These included the Clinical Leadership Programme, the RCN Learning Zone (an e-learning platform developed in collaboration with three higher education institutions), and a comprehensive range of practice-based research programmes. Professor Kitson has had an illustrious academic and professional career. In 1991, she was awarded a Fellowship of the Royal College of Nursing in recognition of her groundbreaking work on Standards of Care. She is also a Supernumerary Fellow of Green College, Oxford, and holds multiple Visiting and Honorary Chairs. In 2001, she was named Distinguished Graduate of the Year by her alma mater, the University of Ulster. Throughout her career, Professor Kitson has published over 100 academic and professional articles and has presented her work on numerous local, national, and international platforms. She has collaborated with the World Health Organization and served as a consultant on international projects for the World Bank. Additionally, she is a Trustee of the Brendoncare Foundation and has previously been a member of the Health Advisory Service 2000 Board and the Policy Advisory Board of the Nuffield Trust.
